unclear.text: Carry-over in the first year: K3 is enforced from 1 January 2028.
readings: U1-a: hours accrued in 2027 and unused on 31 December 2027 must carry into 2028; only enforcement waits
U1-b: K3 applies only to hours accrued from 2028, so an employer may let 2027 hours lapse

unclear.text: Counting employees for K5: the Act does not say whether part-time employees count.
readings: U2-a: every person on the payroll counts as one
U2-b: only employees who average 20 hours a week or more count

a1.text: About 38% of private employees lack paid leave usable for illness, so the term binds for them.

a2.text: Most bound employers comply: payroll vendors build in accrual, and some workers complain.

a3.text: Money wages are fixed in the short run by pay scales, annual raises and collective agreements.

a5.text: Wages above the minimum can adjust over the medium horizon, as raises are set.

a6.text: For the marginal worker and employer, the term is worth less to the worker than it costs the employer: they could have agreed on it and did not.

a7.text: The minimum wage binds for some uncovered workers.

a8.text: Employers can move hours between part-time and full-time staff.

a10.text: Some firms near six employees value staying exempt more than an extra hire.

a12.text: Some existing PTO policies do not meet the K2 conditions (documentation, notice, increments, attendance points).

a20.text: The $3.4 million is new money from the general fund.

a25.text: Owners of firms near six employees know from mid-2026 that the 2026 average decides their 2027 status.
